case_analysis.thread_summary: This is an internal Allion exchange (December 19-23, 2024) where sales staff [PERSON]/Wang forwards a Bluetooth certification quote request from [COMPANY] for an in-vehicle 1DIN audio product (A2DP + AM/FM radio, with HFP and LE Audio planned later) to consultant [PERSON]/Sakai. The product uses a Component-certified BT HCI module and a Component-certified BT stack running on a general-purpose microcontroller, with two destination variants (domestic-only, and domestic+overseas with an external PCB pattern antenna fed from the module via wire). Sakai determines that RF 2-item testing (transmit power, receive sensitivity) is required to validate the custom PCB antenna design for the external-antenna variant, while Profile testing is exempted for profiles covered at the ICS level by the BT stack's Q309493 (Blue SDK Profiles) Component certification. A quote is provided, and a follow-up Q&A sheet is prepared for a customer web meeting (the sheet's contents are in an attachment not reproduced in the email body).
all_questions_found: What testing is required for a product that routes a certified module's antenna signal out to a custom PCB pattern antenna design (for the domestic+overseas variant)?
Is Profile testing required for A2DP (and later HFP/LE Audio) given that the BT stack is already Component-certified under Q309493 (Blue SDK Profiles)?
What is the overall cost quote for registration support, Compliance Folder creation, and required testing for this product?
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The product's antenna configuration differs by destination: domestic-only uses the module's certified antenna as-is, while the domestic+overseas variant routes the module's antenna signal via wire to a custom PCB pattern antenna. This custom antenna design requires RF 2-item testing (transmit power, receive sensitivity) via an SMA-connector coaxial cable near the antenna feed point, requiring an RF-test-modified DUT and test-mode entry procedure. Separately, Profile testing is exempted for profiles (A2DP now, HFP/LE Audio later) that are covered at the ICS level by the BT stack's existing Q309493 (Blue SDK Profiles) Component certification. The quote combines RF 2-item testing (¥200,000), registration support with Multi-Design reference (¥250,000), and Compliance Folder creation (¥150,000), plus the applicant's direct $11,040 SIG fee remittance.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: Test scope was determined per-component: the antenna configuration was evaluated separately from the module/stack's existing certifications - a custom PCB antenna design requires its own RF validation regardless of the module's certification, while profile implementations were checked against the BT stack's existing ICS-level Component certification coverage to determine Profile test exemptions. These determinations together formed the basis for the cost quote (Multi-Design reference registration support, given the multiple destination/antenna variants).
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Treating the module's existing Component certification as covering a custom PCB antenna design would leave that antenna's RF performance unverified for the external-antenna variant, risking registration issues. Assuming all future profile additions (e.g., LE Audio) remain covered by the existing stack certification without re-checking ICS coverage could result in missing required Profile testing later.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For pre-sales quotes involving Component-certified modules/stacks: evaluate antenna design and profile implementation as separate test-scope questions. Custom antenna designs (e.g., PCB pattern antennas fed from a certified module) require their own RF 2-item testing regardless of the module's certification. Profile testing can be exempted only for profiles actually covered at the ICS level by an existing stack Component certification (e.g., Q309493 Blue SDK Profiles) - re-verify coverage when new profiles are planned to be added later.
